title: Seasoned Beef Mince — Nachos & Tacos
description: The foundation of great nachos and tacos — a rich, deeply seasoned beef mince that holds its own under cheese, sour cream, and all the toppings.

ingredients.notes: see recipe, or 1 packet Old El Paso

method.instruction: Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and cook for 3–4 minutes until softened and starting to colour.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add beef mince. Break it up with a wooden spoon or spatula — you want fine crumbles, not chunks. Cook over high heat for 5–7 minutes until well browned. Do not rush this step; good colour on the mince means better flavour.
Drain off excess fat if needed — leave a little for flavour, not a pool of it.
Add tomato paste and stir through for 1–2 minutes until it darkens slightly and coats the mince.
Add taco seasoning and stir through for 30 seconds.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well to combine. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer uncovered for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has reduced and thickened and coats the mince well.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. The mince should be bold and well-seasoned — it needs to hold up under nacho toppings.

notes.title: The Mince Matters
notes.content: Use beef mince at 80/20 fat ratio if possible — the extra fat carries the seasoning better and gives richer flavour. If your mince is very lean, add an extra tablespoon of oil when browning.

notes.title: Nacho Assembly
notes.content: Spread corn chips on an oven tray. Spoon mince generously over the top. Cover with grated cheese. Bake at 200°C for 8–10 minutes until cheese is melted and golden. Top with sour cream, guacamole, jalapeños, and fresh salsa.

notes.title: Taco Assembly
notes.content: Warm taco shells in the oven for 5 minutes at 180°C. Fill generously with mince, then top with shredded lettuce, diced tomato, grated cheese, sour cream, and a squeeze of lime.

notes.title: Make It Go Further
notes.content: A drained 400 g can of kidney beans or black beans stirred in at step 7 stretches the mince to serve 6 and adds great texture and body.

notes.title: Make Ahead
notes.content: The beef mince reheats beautifully. Make a double batch, refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water to loosen.
